_readme: Machine-readable model routing policy for skills/ot-loop. This file is the SINGLE source of
truth for category -> model. CLAUDE.md stays the source of truth for what each model IS
(its cost/intelligence/taste ranking); this file only decides which one a task gets.
Rationale, measurements and the reasons behind each choice: docs/openthrottle/per-task-model-routing.md
Shape: look up lower(tasks.category) in `categories`. A hit gives a tier name; a miss, or a
null/blank category, gives `default`. Resolve the tier in `tiers` to get the `agentModel`
(the value to pass as the Agent tool's `model` parameter) and `recordAs` (the model id to
declare to begin_task_session so attribution and routing agree).
READ_COST_CORRECTLY: In CLAUDE.md's table, every axis is a RANKING where HIGHER = BETTER FOR THE OWNER.
For cost that means HIGHER = CHEAPER. sonnet-5 (cost 5) is the CHEAPEST of the three.
This has been read backwards once, with consequences: ~10 fable subagents were fanned out
over ~60 mechanical component conformances (OT 0f0528ff) and exhausted the org's MONTHLY
spend cap mid-run. The most expensive model was chosen for the most mechanical job because
cost=2 was read as 'cheap'. If you are about to escalate, re-read this paragraph.

claude-sonnet-5.note: Cheapest. CLAUDE.md: bulk/mechanical work, 'effectively free'. Taste 7 already meets CLAUDE.md's user-facing bar of >= 7, so user-facing work does NOT require escalation on taste alone.

claude-opus-5.note: The escalation tier. CLAUDE.md's table names this row opus-4.8 while the harness's current Opus selector resolves to Opus 5; the ranking is what matters here, not the point version. See the naming-drift note in the routing doc.

claude-fable-5.note: Strongest AND most expensive. Never selected by automatic routing — see tiers.review.

default.why: Cheapest model that clears the bar for clear-spec work. The default is deliberately the cheap tier: escalation must be an explicit decision, never what happens when nothing matched.

escalate.why: Intelligence 7 and taste 8 for work whose spec is genuinely open — the task has to decide something, not implement something already decided.

review.why: CLAUDE.md names fable-5 (or opus-4.8) for reviews of plans/implementations, but fable-5 is the most expensive model, so no category maps here. Reaching this tier requires a deliberate per-task decision by the orchestrator or the human, and never applies to a batch.

_why: Routing makes spawning expensive agents trivial, and that has already gone wrong once
(OT 0f0528ff). These bound it. The first two are structural — the loop's shape enforces
them — and the rest are rules a caller has to follow.
maxConcurrentNonDefaultTierAgents_note: STRUCTURALLY ENFORCED today, not an honour-system number: skills/ot-loop runs exactly one
task at a time (its stated invariant) and delegates at most one subagent per task, so 1 is
the shape of the loop rather than a limit bolted onto it.
Any change that introduces intra-task fan-out or parallel task lanes (OT c22e5ba1,
1c0d627a) MUST re-decide this number explicitly for non-default tiers rather than
inheriting whatever concurrency it sets for the cheap tier.
autoRoutedToMostExpensiveTier_note: No category maps to the review tier, so automatic routing can never select fable-5.
This is the load-bearing guardrail: the 0f0528ff failure was an inverted cost axis
producing a fleet of the most expensive model, and that path no longer exists. Even a
cost-axis misreading cannot reach fable through the lookup.
escalationIsPerTask: Escalate one task because that task needs it. NEVER escalate a fleet, a batch, or a plan.
There is no 'this plan is hard, run it all on opus' — the tier is a property of the task.
0f0528ff escalated a batch: ~10 fable subagents over ~60 mechanical component
conformances, which exhausted the org's MONTHLY spend cap mid-run.
splitMixedWorkByDifficulty: When a batch mixes difficulties, split it and route each part. Never route the whole batch
at its hardest item's tier — that is how one genuinely hard task drags 59 mechanical ones
preferFinishingTheMechanicalTail: A finite mechanical tail is cheaper finished in the main loop than re-spawned. Spawning has
a fixed cost per agent and mechanical work does not benefit from a stronger model.
beforeYouEscalate: Re-read READ_COST_CORRECTLY at the top of this file. Higher cost number = CHEAPER.
If you are escalating more than one task at a time, stop — see escalationIsPerTask.

notKeyedOn.task_tags: Rejected for v1. task_tags.dimension is CHECK-constrained to ('domain','phase') (migration 064), so a routing dimension needs a migration, and task_tags is sparsely populated compared to tasks.category (84% populated). Revisit only if category proves too coarse in practice.
notKeyedOn.tag_action_rules: Rejected. It has the right extension seam but the wrong semantics: rules are fingerprinted one-application-per-(rule, plan) and 'Actions are NEVER undone' — un-matching only flips a ledger row to 'orphaned'. Model routing must be re-decided fresh on every run.
